title: Tata Motors Ltd - 544569 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Tata Motors Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 22% YoY to Rs 24,500 crore with EBITDA margin at 13.9%, but management guided only to single-digit Q1 growth amid commodity and diesel risks.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter of the year on volume and price, with wholesales of about 131.8K units (up 25% YoY) and standalone EBIT margin of 12.1%. FY26 standalone EBIT crossed 11% for the first time and free cash flow reached about Rs 9,200 crore. Management flagged a sharp commodity cost headwind (about 100 bps in Q4 and significantly higher in Q1 FY27), took only a 2% price increase in April, and said it will not pass through the full cost increase. Iveco deal closure has slipped to Q2 FY27 pending French and Spanish financial regulatory approvals.

segments.name: Trucks (HCV / ILMCV)
segments.commentary: Management cited highest HCV offtake market share in a decade; ILMCV (5-19 t) showed the highest growth rates through the year. 17 next-gen trucks launched at start of Q4; entire truck range now meets European cabin safety standards.

segments.name: Buses
segments.commentary: Enters FY27 with a solid government order book; 5,000 bus orders secured from STUs during FY26. Management is focused on rebuilding share on a profitable basis; the company is not bidding aggressively on EV bus tenders, calling current quotes unsustainable.

segments.name: SCV Pickup / Small CV
segments.commentary: Ace Pro (launched June 2025) and Intra EV drove volume momentum; EV penetration in SCV pickup rose to about 7% in the last 1-2 months vs about 4% for FY26, with management expecting higher single-digit penetration.

segments.name: Parts & Services / Fleet Edge / Smart City
segments.commentary: Parts and service growth sustained at a higher trajectory; Fleet Edge subscription renewals almost doubled from Q1 to Q4. Smart City has 3,815+ cumulative e-buses deployed, ~59 crore km run, and above 96% uptime.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Largest-ever order of 70,000 Yodha and Ultra T.7 units for Indonesia secured in February; first shipment already at sea after homologation. No shipments to Middle East for the last two months; Sri Lanka under pressure from fuel availability.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 revenue growth guided at single digit, 'if not more', YoY, with management declining to give full-year visibility and pointing to quarter-by-quarter guidance.
Commodity headwind: about 100 bps impact in Q4 FY26, with significantly higher impact expected in Q1 FY27 (steel, aluminium, copper, precious metals, rupee depreciation).
A 2% price increase taken in April 2026; management does not intend to pass through the full commodity increase and will offset through cost levers.
EBITDA margin guidance is 'teens' (corrected from 'mid-teens' on the call), held quarter-by-quarter given cost headwinds.
FY27 investment spend (R&D plus capex) expected broadly in line with FY26 (Rs 3,000 crore); capex guided at 2% to 4% of revenue.

Iveco transaction closure expected in Q2 FY27; financing via bridge loan then refinancing, with the equity/debt mix still open. Final dividend of Rs 4 per share (about Rs 1,500 crore cash outflow) is subject to shareholder approval.
capex_capacity: FY26 total investment spend about Rs 3,000 crore: R&D about Rs 1,700 crore and capex plus other investments about Rs 1,100 crore; within the 2%-4% of revenue guidance band.
EV ramp: Intra EV in only its second month of production; management plans to ramp gradually to meet demand.
Electric trucks: 55-ton electric tractor deliveries started with BillionE Mobility; MoU with VOC port (Tamil Nadu) for 40 H2-ICE trucks trials; about 250 electric bus orders received.
Iveco acquisition pending approvals; management said most regulatory approvals are received, with only French and Spanish financial regulatory approvals outstanding.
demand_pricing: Industry TIV grew 19% YoY in Q4 FY26 while Tata Motors volumes grew 25%; FY26 TIV grew 12.5% vs company growth of 11.6%.
H1 FY26 was muted (Operation Sindoor sentiment and early monsoon); H2 recovered on GST 2.0-led consumption, with Q4 the standout quarter.
April 2026 industry volumes saw healthy double-digit growth; management says roughly half of May is in and momentum is intact.
Management claims ASPs are rising segment by segment (trucks up YoY); the blended ASP decline is attributed to higher van mix and almost no electric bus sales in FY26.
Diesel is the key monitorable: it is 30-50% of total cost of ownership for transporters; diesel sales rose 8% YoY in March but April was about flat YoY per management.
Heavy-duty customers are postponing purchases toward month-end amid diesel uncertainty; smaller vehicles see lower uncertainty.
E-way bill generation grew 15% YoY in Q4 and 12% YoY in April 2026 per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 growth outlook for MHCV and LCV, and how much risk do fuel price hikes pose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a single-digit Q1 growth 'if not more' and will guide quarter by quarter; diesel prices are the key monitorable as they drive 30-50% of TCO.

qa_highlights.question: How much commodity cost pressure is expected in Q1, how much is being passed on, and what drives margins from here?
qa_highlights.answer: About 100 bps hit in Q4 with a significantly higher impact in Q1; a 2% price increase was taken in April, with the rest absorbed through cost levers to protect demand.

qa_highlights.question: When will the 70,000-unit Indonesia order be executed, and will it finish in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Product is homologated in Indonesia and first shipment is at sea; ramp-up to be rapid, with delivery timeline to be discussed in future quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is causing the Iveco closure delay, and how does the activist stake affect the deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Most approvals are in; the last two financial regulatory approvals (France and Spain) are pending, pushing closure into Q2 FY27. Management is confident the investor will support the offer.

qa_highlights.question: Are ASPs falling due to discounting or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says segment ASPs are rising; the decline in blended ASP reflects higher van volumes and minimal electric bus sales versus last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company not participating in EV bus tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Quotes in recent CESL tenders are seen as unsustainable; the company was near L2 in one sub-part of the first tender and is pursuing corporate and intercity EV bus demand instead.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 4Q working-capital inflow seasonality still hold, and what is FY27 capex guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 working capital was managed more evenly through the year, with YTD cash flow positive after Q2; FY27 capex guided at 2%-4% of revenue.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (steel, aluminium, copper, precious metals) and rupee depreciation, with Q1 FY27 impact expected to be significantly higher than Q4's 100 bps.
Diesel prices and their effect on transporter economics and heavy-duty purchase timing; April diesel sales were about flat YoY.
Middle East shipments halted for two months; Sri Lanka fuel shortage; geopolitical disruption to export routes.
Iveco deal: pending French and Spanish financial regulatory approvals, financing mix (equity vs debt) still undecided, and an activist hedge fund's stake build (6-7%).
Electric bus business: company is holding back from tenders, leaving it out of the EV bus segment for now; EV pickup penetration needs to hold near 7%.
Management has halted its quarterly transporter sentiment survey and is revisiting the methodology.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 execution and structural margin gains, but cautious and non-committal on FY27: management repeatedly declined multi-quarter guidance and framed outlook as quarter-by-quarter, citing diesel and commodity uncertainty.

growth.why: Management guided Q1 FY27 volume/revenue growth to single digit 'if not more' and declined full-year visibility, with commodity and diesel headwinds; backing is partial (5,000 bus orders, 70,000-unit Indonesia order, 2% April price hike, Intra EV ramp), with no explicit new capacity sized in the brief and capex guided at 2-4% of revenue.
